title: Setting Up Your Environment
description: Install Python, create a virtual environment, and install Django.

slides.title: Why Virtual Environments? 🧪
slides.content:
# Isolate Your Projects

Imagine you have two projects: one needs Django 4.0 and another needs Django 5.0. Without isolation, you'd have to constantly reinstall. **A virtual environment** is like a **clean room** – each project has its own set of packages, no conflicts!

We'll use `venv` (built into Python 3).

slides.title: Creating a Virtual Environment
slides.content: Open your terminal (command prompt) and navigate to where you want your project. Then run:
slides.codeSnippet:
# On Windows
python -m venv myenv

# On macOS/Linux
python3 -m venv myenv

slides.title: Activating the Environment
slides.content: Activation tells your terminal to use the isolated Python and pip from that folder.

quizData.question: What is the main benefit of using a virtual environment?

options.text: It makes your code run faster
It isolates project dependencies to avoid version conflicts
It automatically deploys your app to the cloud

quizData.explanation: Virtual environments create isolated spaces for each project, ensuring packages don't clash across projects.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Keep your environment clean

Always **activate** your virtual environment before working on a project. When you're done, type `deactivate` to exit.
